_readme: THE CAPABILITY REGISTER — [pipeline C-1] Private/requirements/ (was pipeline/02-shared-chassis.md, folded into the JSON spec 2026-08-15)
The complete set of non-app-specific capabilities the factory provides: what it is, which package
owns it, which SEAM INTERFACE (file + symbol + methods) others code against, and who consumes it.
Why it exists: 'every capability' cannot be checked against a list that does not exist. THREE
notification implementations were written because nobody had a place to look that would have said
one already existed. The third is still in the tree -- see violations on `notifications`.
THE ARCHITECTURE THIS ENCODES: packages/core DECLARES the contracts; other packages IMPLEMENT them.
So `seams` are the interfaces a package declares, and `implementsSeams` names contracts declared
elsewhere that it satisfies. v1 of this file pointed every seam at a package barrel file, which
· every packages/* dir on disk has an entry, and every path named here exists
· every declared seam SYMBOL really appears in the file that claims it
· every declared seam METHOD really appears in that interface  [decision item 12]
· consumers verified in BOTH directions against real pubspecs
· no registered seam may be implemented under apps/ unless declared as a violation  [C-3, widened]
VIOLATIONS ARE DECLARED, DATED AND PRINTED ON EVERY RUN. A known gap that nobody sees becomes
permanent. Each names why it is not yet fixed and what would unblock it.

_why: [pipeline C-8] EVERY VENDOR SATISFIES THE PORTABILITY CHECKLIST, not just 'behind a seam'.
Top-down from the charter kept 'behind a seam' and silently dropped the rest -- which is how a
seam ends up LOOKING like portability while a vendor swap still needs a store release.
SIX PARTS, not four. The requirement's own title says 'four-part' and portability-standard.md's
checklist lists SIX; the lock resolved the contradiction to six, the checklist being the primary
record. Four are machine-checkable and BLOCK; two are judgement and PRINT:
1 openProtocol   PRINTS  -- does it speak a standard, or is there a compatibility layer
2 seam           CHECKED -- the named symbol must exist where it claims to
3 configKeyed    CHECKED -- every surface is runtime-config-keyed, or compile-time WITH a
reason. 'No release to repoint' is the property.
4 ownTheRecord   PRINTS  -- the app depends on OUR record, not the vendor's
5 exportPath     CHECKED -- the cited runbook/script must exist on disk
6 exitPlan       CHECKED -- a named alternative and its swap cost, non-empty
SURFACES ARE DERIVED FROM THE TREE, never typed here, and from FOUR sources because any one
alone is blind (all four verified 2026-07-28):
a. `*.fromEnvironment('KEY')` in Dart -- MULTILINE. A line-based grep finds 2 of the 11 that
exist, because dart format wraps the literal onto the next line. UPDATE_URL is one it misses.
b. `interface Env` in services/*/src/types.ts -- REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_SECRET lived ONLY here, so
without it RevenueCat, the amendment's own example, was invisible. (2026-09-16: that secret
retired with the legacy route; the platform verifier's REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET is
read dynamically, like PADDLE_NOTIFICATION_SECRET, and is not an Env key.)
c. wrangler `binding` keys AND `ratelimits[].name` -- ratelimits uses `name`, not `binding`, so
a binding-only scan cannot see EVENTS_LIMITER.
d. `triggers.crons` -- a schedule is an external surface too; a dead cron looks like a live one.
Every derived surface must be claimed by exactly one vendor or declared a non-vendor surface.
That is what stops a new vendor arriving unnoticed -- the failure this whole register exists for.
SCOPE: services, not libraries. portability-standard.md's checklist opens 'before adopting any new
SERVICE'. Dart package dependencies are [2]C-5's limb (c), which already stops an app importing a
vendor SDK the seam wraps; duplicating them here would be two lists to keep in step.

supabase.surface: Portfolio-wide identity/auth (project Cross_Platform_Auth) and the Postgres behind it.
supabase.stickiness: ★★★ — portability-standard.md names RLS coupling as one of three sticky points.
supabase.openProtocol: YES — OIDC/JWKS for tokens and plain Postgres underneath. Verification is against standard JWKS claims, not a Supabase SDK call, which is what makes the identity provider swappable.

configKeyed.detail: URL and anon key are dart-defines with compiled-in fallbacks, and the Worker reads SUPABASE_URL from its own env — repointing needs no app release.

supabase.ownTheRecord: YES — entitlements and app state live in OUR D1, keyed on the standard `sub` claim. The app depends on our record, not Supabase's.

exportPath.detail: pg_dump via the Supabase dashboard/API; the schema is plain Postgres with no proprietary types.

exitPlan.alternative: any OIDC provider (Auth0, Clerk, self-hosted Keycloak) behind the same AuthRepository seam
exitPlan.swapCost: Medium — JWKS verification is standard, so the cost is re-issuing sessions and migrating the user table, NOT rewriting the app.

cloudflare.surface: Workers runtime, D1 (platform_db, subscriptiontracker_db), KV (config, JWKS cache, signups, the signed-out-session list), the events/config/money rate-limiters, and ONE R2 bucket. ~~NO R2 surface as of 2026-08-01~~ — WITHDRAWN 2026-09-05: `nikatru-backups` is bound for the nightly off-vendor export of D1 and KV (research/revamp-2026-09-05/06 sec 4.2). It is the LEAST sticky surface here, not a new dependency — R2 is S3-compatible, so rclone reads it today and would read a replacement tomorrow, and the objects are gzipped JSON lines that nothing but our own script parses.
cloudflare.stickiness: ★★★ — portability-standard.md names KV/DO as a sticky point.
cloudflare.openProtocol: PARTIAL — D1 is SQLite dialect and R2 is S3-compatible, both portable. KV and the rate-limiter are proprietary; the crons are a Workers-only scheduler. This is the honest weak spot, and it is why the stickiness is ★★★.

configKeyed.detail: Bindings are wrangler config, not code — swapping a database or bucket is a config edit and a deploy, never an app release.

cloudflare.ownTheRecord: YES — D1 IS our record. The risk here is not losing the record to a vendor, it is the SQLite dialect and the KV semantics.

exportPath.detail: PUBLIC, CHECKABLE EVIDENCE: the D1 schema is plain SQL migrations in this repo — that IS the export shape, and it is why a D1 export lands in any SQLite or Postgres. R2 is S3-compatible so rclone moves it. KV has no bulk export primitive; the mitigation is that KV holds only last-good config and a JWKS cache, both regenerable, so nothing in KV is a record of record. ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-01: the FINDING of 2026-07-28 — the subscriptiontracker-api `EXPORTS` R2 binding declared in types.ts and referenced NOWHERE in the code, a bound bucket with no writer, the same fail-closed-with-no-open-path shape [2]C-6 exists to catch — was routed to stage 4 and executed there. The binding and its type declaration are gone ([4]B-18), and tooling/ci/assert-platform-register.mjs now fails on ANY binding in ANY wrangler config in the repo (brick template included) with no resolved reader, so this cannot recur silently. ⚠️ The BUCKET is still in the account: deleting it is destructive and is the owner's. There is therefore NO R2 surface in this list today, which is correct — the rule is ONE portfolio bucket bound in services/platform when object storage is genuinely needed, addressed by an `<app_id>/` prefix.

exitPlan.alternative: Postgres/Neon + S3 + any Node host behind the same Worker handlers
exitPlan.swapCost: High for KV/DO semantics, Low for D1/R2. Deliberately kept: nothing durable lives in KV.

cloudflare-turnstile.surface: Cloudflare Turnstile — the bot-detection challenge on the four gated auth screens (sign-in, sign-up, forgot-password, resend-verification). TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY is the PUBLIC site key, passed as a dart-define; the secret half lives on the auth box as CAPTCHA_SECRET and never reaches this repo.
cloudflare-turnstile.stickiness: ★☆☆ — one widget, one public key, one server-side verify URL. The lowest-stickiness vendor in this register.
cloudflare-turnstile.openProtocol: NO — the widget script, the token format and the siteverify endpoint are all proprietary to Cloudflare. That sounds worse than it is: hCaptcha and reCAPTCHA expose the SAME shape (embed a script keyed by a public site key, receive an opaque token, POST it to the vendor's verify endpoint), so the interface is de-facto uniform across the alternatives even though no standard names it.

configKeyed.reason: TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY is a --dart-define, so repointing it is a WEB BUILD, not a config edit — this vendor is the exception to the runtime rule the other rows keep, and it is recorded rather than hidden. Two things bound the cost: `web` is the only channel with served: true, so there are no installed clients holding a compiled-in key; and the key is PUBLIC by design, so a rotation is a redeploy and never a secret-handling exercise. ⚠️ It stops being cheap at the first store release, when installed clients would hold the old key until they update. ⏱ APPENDED 2026-09-15: that warning no longer binds — [ADR 084] (owner, "Store builds skip it") keeps the key out of every store build by design, graded by assert-store-build-config.mjs (web lanes MUST pass it, store lanes MUST NOT), so no installed client holds it and a rotation stays a web redeploy.

cloudflare-turnstile.ownTheRecord: NOT APPLICABLE, AND THAT IS THE POINT — Turnstile holds no record of ours. It answers one question (is this caller a bot) and keeps nothing we would need back. This row exists to say that explicitly: a vendor that stores nothing still has to be claimed, or an unreviewed dependency is indistinguishable from one nobody has looked at.

exportPath.detail: NO EXPORT PATH, BECAUSE THERE IS NOTHING TO EXPORT. Deliberately no `path`: the field is present so the checklist is answered, and empty so it cannot be read as an untested exit. Contrast the `cloudflare` row above, whose exportPath cites services/platform/migrations because D1 IS our record — filing Turnstile under that vendor would have made that sentence cover a surface it says nothing about, which is why this is a separate row rather than one more name in cloudflare.surfaces.

exitPlan.alternative: hCaptcha (drop-in: same public-site-key + opaque-token + siteverify shape), or GoTrue's own rate limiting alone
exitPlan.swapCost: LOW — replace the body of TurnstileGate, swap one dart-define, and change GOTRUE_SECURITY_CAPTCHA_PROVIDER on the auth box. ⚠️ The cost that is NOT low is the store declarations: the current implementation reaches Turnstile through cloudflare_turnstile → flutter_inappwebview, a linked binary that carries sworn rows in ios-appstore/privacy-manifest.json and android-play/data-safety.json. A provider swap that changes the webview dependency changes those sworn answers too, so the exit is cheap in code and NOT free in paperwork.

revenuecat.surface: Subscription entitlement provider — the client SDK key. (The server webhook secret left this list 2026-09-16 with the legacy bearer route; the platform money door's signing secret is a registry-declared destination secret, as Paddle's is.)
revenuecat.stickiness: ★★★★ — payments, the stickiest point the standard names.
revenuecat.openProtocol: NO — payment APIs are proprietary and there is no standard to speak. This is precisely why part 4 carries the weight for this vendor.

configKeyed.detail: Client key is a dart-define with a fallback; the webhook secret is Worker env. Neither requires an app release to rotate.

revenuecat.ownTheRecord: YES, AND IT IS THE WHOLE STRATEGY — entitlements live in OUR table fed by a per-provider adapter, so the payment vendor is swappable even though payment APIs are not. This is the one line the audit note said to carry forward verbatim.

exportPath.detail: Entitlements are ours in D1 and export with it. RevenueCat itself holds no record we depend on.

exitPlan.alternative: Paddle (the locked MoR, ADR 004) or direct store IAP, behind the same entitlement adapter
exitPlan.swapCost: Medium — a new adapter and a webhook, but no app data migration, because we own the record.

revenuecat.note: ⬜ NOT YET LIVE. Nobody can pay NIKATRU today; stage 5 owns the money rail. ⚠️ 2026-08-01: the CLIENT rail now exists too (packages/purchases + the brick wiring), so what remains is not any code. — CORRECTION 2026-08-28: that sentence ended ‘so what remains is the seller account itself (A-1), not any code’, and the seller account is no longer what remains: the Paddle account went LIVE 2026-08-11 ([ADR 044]). What still stops a payment is `paywall.enabled: false` for every app in services/platform/src/app-config-data.json plus the unset PADDLE_NOTIFICATION_SECRET — so the opening sentence of this note, ‘Nobody can pay NIKATRU today’, is still TRUE, for different reasons than it was written for. Recorded now because the surfaces already exist in the tree, and a vendor whose keys are wired before its checklist is exactly the adoption-without-review this requirement stops.

paddle.surface: MERCHANT OF RECORD for web/desktop — the legal seller, which remits global VAT/GST on our behalf. The surface in this repo is ONE value: the per-destination webhook notification secret. — CORRECTION 2026-08-25: it is TWO. `PADDLE_API_KEY`, the seller API key `POST /v1/checkout` creates a transaction with, is the second, and it was invisible to this register rather than absent from the tree: `routes/checkout.ts` read it as `(c.env as unknown as Record<string, string | undefined>)['PADDLE_API_KEY']`, so it appeared in no `interface Env` and this guard’s derivation could not see it. Declaring the binding surfaced it. Both are Worker SECRETS (`wrangler secret put`), never committed vars; both are OWNER-GATED on the same seller account (OWNER_QUEUE A-1); and neither changes anything else in this record — the seam, the export path and the exit plan below are about the entitlement the rail produces, not about how many credentials open the door. The key is additionally world-bound: checkout.ts refuses a `pdl_sdbx_apikey_` prefix on a `live` deploy and vice versa ([5]M-12).
paddle.stickiness: ★★★★ — payments, the stickiest point the portability standard names. Mitigated to the extent it can be: the entitlement RECORD is ours, and the rail is one interface with per-provider adapters.
paddle.openProtocol: NO — payment APIs are proprietary and there is no standard to speak. Which is exactly why parts 2 and 4 carry the weight here: the SIGNATURE SCHEME is proprietary and lives in one adapter file, and the entitlement it produces is written in our own vocabulary into our own table.

seam.note: [ADR 004] specifies this seam by name: 'build the payment webhook provider-agnostic (MoRWebhookVerifier interface + per-provider signature adapters) so the choice can flip with zero app changes'. Every Paddle-specific fact — the header name, the HMAC construction, the status vocabulary, the id prefixes — lives in services/platform/src/lib/mor/paddle.ts and nowhere else, and each one carries the developer.paddle.com URL it was verified against.

configKeyed.detail: The notification secret is a Worker secret (`wrangler secret put`), never a committed var and never a compile-time define. Rotating it, or switching the whole rail to a different merchant of record (NOT Lemon Squeezy — retired 2026-08-09 by [ADR 039] D4; see exitPlan below), is a secret change plus a registry line — no app release, and no already-shipped client is affected, because clients never talk to the rail.

paddle.ownTheRecord: YES, AND IT IS THE WHOLE STRATEGY — the entitlement lives in OUR platform_db, keyed by our own (user_id, app_id, entitlement), written in OUR vocabulary by a per-provider adapter. Paddle holds the buyer relationship and the money; it holds no record the apps depend on. The one thing that is genuinely theirs and not ours is the CUSTOMER: a buyer's payment method and billing history stay with the merchant of record, which is the deal being made when someone else is the legal seller.

exportPath.detail: PUBLIC, CHECKABLE EVIDENCE: 0004_money_rail.sql IS the export shape. Every fact the rail depends on is a column in plain SQL in this repo — the provider, the environment, the provider's own ids, its status verbatim, both dates, the revocation reason — plus `provider_notifications`, which keeps every notification byte for byte. So the migration path OUT of Paddle is: point the new rail's adapter at the same table. The verbatim store also means a derivation defect is repairable from data we hold rather than from data we would have to ask a vendor for.

exitPlan.alternative: A successor merchant of record — FastSpring / Polar / Creem / direct Stripe plus a tax engine — or an India-native MoR, behind the same MoRWebhookVerifier. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-28: this read 'Lemon Squeezy (the parallel rail [ADR 004] applies for on the same day, PayPal payout from India)'. [ADR 039] D4 (2026-08-09) RETIRED that clause of [ADR 004] — the parallel application was never evidenced and the product is sunsetting into Stripe. WHICH successor is a queued owner decision and is deliberately not answered by putting a name here; tooling/legal/provider-register.json's `lemon-squeezy` row carries the same retirement.
exitPlan.swapCost: Medium — one adapter file and one destination secret. No app release, no client change, and NO DATA MIGRATION, because the entitlement table is ours and speaks nobody's vocabulary but our own.

paddle.note: 🟢 THE SELLER ACCOUNT IS LIVE — CORRECTED 2026-08-28. This note read, verbatim: '⬜ NOT YET LIVE, AND THE GAP IS ONE SIGNUP. The rail is built, tested and mounted; PADDLE_NOTIFICATION_SECRET does not exist because it can only be generated in the Paddle seller console, which needs the seller account — OWNER_QUEUE A-1, PENDING.' THE SIGNUP HALF IS DONE: [ADR 044], LOCKED 2026-08-11, evidences a PRODUCTION credential — PADDLE_API_KEY_LIVE (prefix `pdl_live_apikey_`) authenticating against api.paddle.com, 403’d by the SANDBOX host with the same key (which is what proves it is production), and a live POST /transactions returning 201 with txn_01kzs3qcvryq785t7shpq5d7wj. tooling/legal/provider-register.json’s paddle row is `status: live` for the same reason. ⚠️ WHAT REMAINS IS THE DESTINATION SECRET, NOT AN ACCOUNT: PADDLE_NOTIFICATION_SECRET is generated per notification-destination in the seller console and set with `wrangler secret put`, and a Worker secret is invisible to every guard in this tree — so until it is set POST /v1/money/paddle answers 503, and tooling/ci/assert-mor-adapters.mjs PRINTS that one gap on every run rather than failing the build over work only the owner can do. [ADR 004]’s 2026-07-24 sequencing constraint — apply only after a reviewable product with a live paywall and complete legal pages exists — is HISTORICAL now that the application has landed; it is kept because it explains the date. ⛔ AND `live` HERE IS PER CHANNEL: Apple and Google Play remain the merchant of record on their own in-app purchases ([ADR 039] D1, LOCKED 2026-08-09).

razorpay.surface: The INDIA SELLER's payment GATEWAY. [ADR 076] §10 makes Nikatru the seller of record for India domestic sales, with Razorpay as the gateway rather than a merchant of record, and [ADR 094] routes apps.gov.in and India extension buyers through it. The surface in this repo is three Worker secrets: RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET, which the razorpayVerifier checks the X-Razorpay-Signature HMAC with, and the API key pair RAZORPAY_KEY_ID / RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET a checkout creator will authenticate with. Declared in `interface Env` on 2026-09-24 (O-RAZORPAY-CHECKOUT-ADAPTER), which is what makes them derived surfaces this vendor claims.
razorpay.stickiness: ★★★★ — payments, the stickiest point the portability standard names. Mitigated the same way as paddle: the entitlement RECORD is ours, and the rail is one interface with per-provider adapters.
razorpay.openProtocol: NO — payment APIs are proprietary and there is no standard to speak. The signature scheme (HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body, in X-Razorpay-Signature) and the event-id header live in one adapter file, services/platform/src/lib/mor/razorpay.ts, and what the rail produces is written in our own vocabulary into our own table.

seam.note: The same seam paddle and revenuecat sit behind ([ADR 004]). Every Razorpay-specific fact — the signature header, the HMAC construction, the `x-razorpay-event-id` header the door reads through `eventIdHeader` — lives in services/platform/src/lib/mor/razorpay.ts and nowhere else, quoted from the razorpay.com page it was read from.

configKeyed.detail: All three are Worker secrets (`wrangler secret put`), never committed vars and never compile-time defines; tooling/ci/assert-money-config.mjs fails the build on a destination secret in any `vars` block, top level or environment. The owner pastes them, test mode and live, through the vault one-command. Rotating one is a secret change: no app release, and no shipped client talks to the rail.

razorpay.ownTheRecord: YES — the same strategy as paddle. What this rail produces will be written into OUR platform_db in OUR vocabulary by the adapter, and `provider_notifications` keeps every notification byte for byte under (provider, provider_event_id), where this rail's event id is the `x-razorpay-event-id` header the door persists. Razorpay holds the buyer's payment method and its own payment record.

exportPath.detail: The same PUBLIC, CHECKABLE export shape as paddle: 0004_money_rail.sql's columns plus `provider_notifications`, the verbatim store. Leaving Razorpay means pointing another adapter at the same table.

exitPlan.alternative: Cashfree, the alternative [ADR 076] names in its rider, which is not withdrawn — behind the same MoRWebhookVerifier seam.
exitPlan.swapCost: Medium — one adapter file, one registry line, its secrets and a checkout creator. No app release, no client change and no data migration, because the entitlement table is ours.

razorpay.note: ⬜ NOT YET LIVE. `parse` refuses every body (the payload shape is not yet read from a real event), no checkout creator exists, and all three secrets are unset, so POST /v1/money/razorpay answers 503 before it reads anything. Recorded now because the names are declared in the tree, and a vendor whose keys are declared before its checklist is exactly the adoption-without-review this register stops.

glitchtip.surface: Crash and error reporting sink (self-hostable Sentry-protocol server).
glitchtip.stickiness: ★ — deliberately the least sticky choice available.
glitchtip.openProtocol: YES — speaks the Sentry protocol, so the sentry_flutter SDK talks to it unmodified and any Sentry-protocol sink is a drop-in.

configKeyed.reason: OWNER DECISION 2026-07-27: GLITCHTIP_DSN stays compile-time while UPDATE_URL moves to runtime. A DSN is a build-identity fact — a build reports as itself — and routing crash reports through runtime config would mean a broken config could silently disable the very channel that reports it being broken.

glitchtip.ownTheRecord: N/A — telemetry is a diagnostic stream, not a record the app depends on. Losing history costs insight, never correctness.

exportPath.detail: Self-hosted; the whole instance is ours, and the runbook covers the server backup.

exitPlan.alternative: Sentry SaaS, or any Sentry-protocol server — the DSN is the only thing that changes ⏱ APPENDED 2026-09-14 (O-GITHUB-SCHEDULER): the second surface, PLATFORM_CRON_HEARTBEAT_URL, is a GlitchTip Heartbeat monitor URL the platform Worker POSTs at the end of every cron firing (services/platform/src/scheduled.ts platformCronBeat). It is not the Sentry protocol but something plainer: a bodyless POST to a URL, the dead-man switch shape every uptime service offers, so the swap is one Worker secret and no code. ⏱ APPENDED 2026-09-18 (O-LAPTOP-ROUTINES-DIE-OVERNIGHT): OPS_WATCHDOG_HEARTBEAT_URL is the same dead-man shape for the ops watchdog (services/platform/src/scheduled.ts opsWatchdogJob), and GLITCHTIP_TOKEN / GLITCHTIP_URL let that job READ monitor status over GlitchTip's REST API (src/ops-watchdog.ts checkGlitchtipMonitors) — the one GlitchTip-specific call, a single GET per declared monitor, so a swap rewrites one function.
exitPlan.swapCost: Low — one config value, because the protocol is open.

github.surface: GitHub Actions workflow dispatch — the alarm clock's outbound leg. The `platform` Worker POSTs `workflow_dispatch` so that a Cloudflare cron, not GitHub's own scheduler, decides WHEN a workflow runs. [research/76 §C] Phase 1.
github.stickiness: ★★★★★ — the stickiest entry in this register, and it is written down rather than implied. GitHub holds the repositories, CI, the release lanes, the issue-based alert chain and the RECORD every duty row reads. ⚠️ WHAT THIS SURFACE ADDS IS NOT NEW LOCK-IN — it is one more call into a dependency the whole pipeline already rests on. Declaring it here makes that dependency countable instead of assumed, which is the only thing this register can honestly buy on a vendor nobody is leaving.
github.openProtocol: NO — `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{file}/dispatches` is GitHub-specific. But the CALLER is one fetch with a JSON body, and the shape is common to every forge with an API-triggered pipeline (GitLab pipeline triggers, Forgejo/Gitea actions), so the port is a URL and a header rather than a rewrite.

configKeyed.reason: A Worker secret (`wrangler secret put GITHUB_DISPATCH_TOKEN`), never a committed var — it can push work into two public repositories. 🔴 ABSENT IS A RECORDED STATE, NOT A SKIP: the limb writes one `cron_heartbeat` row per target saying the credential is missing, because a dispatcher that quietly does nothing is indistinguishable from one that is working.

github.ownTheRecord: PARTLY, AND THE GAP IS PHASE 2. The record that the dispatch HAPPENED is `platform_db.cron_heartbeat`, which is ours and is read by tooling/ops/check-heartbeats.mjs from outside Cloudflare. The record that the dispatched WORKFLOW ran is GitHub's own run history — which is the circularity research/76 §C exists to break, and the reason Phase 2 repoints the duty readers at D1 rather than merely repointing the trigger.

exportPath.detail: cron_heartbeat is a D1 table in this repository's own migrations; the dispatch record leaves with the database, not with GitHub.

exitPlan.alternative: The dispatched workflow's own `schedule:` block, which is deliberately KEPT as a backstop and is what evidences the cadence today — so losing this surface degrades timeliness and loses nothing else.
exitPlan.swapCost: Low — one URL, one header set, one status code. The fallback needs no change at all because it was never removed.

apple.surface: ⏱ 2026-09-16 · O-SIWA-TOKEN-NOT-REVOKED-ON-DELETE. IDENTITY PROVIDER for Sign in with Apple, on ONE call: `POST https://appleid.apple.com/auth/revoke`, which the account deletion makes so Apple stops listing this app as connected. The sign-in itself does NOT go through these surfaces — it is Supabase's OAuth flow — so what is claimed here is the revocation only.
apple.stickiness: ★★★ — not a swappable vendor at all: it is Apple's own identity, required by Apple's own review rules for any app offering Sign in with Apple. The bounded part is that nothing but the revoke call depends on it, so the cost of Apple changing it is one module.
apple.openProtocol: PARTIAL — the call is plain OAuth 2.0 token revocation (RFC 7009 shape: `client_id`, `client_secret`, `token`, `token_type_hint`, form-encoded, 200 with no body), but the `client_secret` is an Apple-specific ES256 JWT (`iss` Team ID, `sub` client id, `aud` https://appleid.apple.com, `kid` the key id), so a generic OAuth client cannot be pointed at it unchanged.

configKeyed.reason: Four Worker secrets, owner-provisioned with `wrangler secret put`. The private key is the `.p8` Apple issues ONCE in the developer portal; no agent creates or downloads it. Absent, the revoke returns `blocked`, the deletion stays 202 `erasure_pending` and the identity is not deleted — a refusal, never a skip.

apple.ownTheRecord: N/A — there is no record of ours here. The only thing held is the user's own Apple refresh token (platform_db.provider_tokens with provider = 'apple', copied there from apple_provider_tokens by 0016), and it exists to be destroyed: the revoke consumes it and the row goes.

exportPath.detail: NO EXPORT PATH, BECAUSE THERE IS NOTHING TO EXPORT, and the missing `path` is deliberate — the same shape cloudflare-turnstile uses. Nothing of ours lives at Apple through this surface: the single call is a DESTRUCTION (revoke the user's token) and Apple answers it with no body. The one value that exists is the user's own Apple refresh token, held in platform_db.provider_tokens, which exports with that database's migrations and is deleted the moment the revoke succeeds.

exitPlan.alternative: None, and that is the honest answer: if the product offers Sign in with Apple, Apple is the revocation authority. Dropping Sign in with Apple as a sign-in option is what retires this vendor, and it retires the whole surface with it.
exitPlan.swapCost: Low in code (one module, one call, four secrets) and not a decision about code: it is the decision to keep or drop Sign in with Apple.

resend.surface: ⏱ 2026-09-18 · O-PLAY-AI-CONTENT-REPORTING. Transactional email from a Worker — ONE use today: the support notice that an in-app AI content report arrived. Resend already carries the portfolio's auth mail through Supabase SMTP ([ADR 029], tooling/mail-transport.json), but that path is configured in Supabase, not in this tree; this record is for the first code in services/ that calls Resend's API itself. The auth+alerts container ([ADR 041]), sender alerts@mail.nikatru.com.
resend.stickiness: ★ — the least sticky kind of vendor: one POST with a from, a to, a subject and a text body. No template, no audience, no stored record we read back.
resend.openProtocol: PARTIAL — the API is Resend's own, but what it sends is plain SMTP mail from our own DKIM-signed subdomain (mail.nikatru.com), and the same message could leave through Resend's SMTP relay or any other provider without the recipient seeing a difference.

seam.note: Every Resend fact — the URL, the Bearer header, the body shape — lives in this one function. The route calls notifyReport and knows nothing about who delivers the mail.

configKeyed.reason: A Worker SECRET (`wrangler secret put RESEND_API_KEY`), never a committed var. It is the auth+alerts container's key — the same credential as the vault's SMTP_PASS — so it ROTATES TOGETHER with Supabase smtp_pass and Box A's EMAIL_URL. Absent, the notice is skipped and the report is still stored: nothing needs a release to repoint.

resend.ownTheRecord: YES — the report is ours, in platform_db.content_reports (migration 0013). Resend holds only its own log of the notice it delivered, which carries a report id, an app, a reason and a time — no user content. Losing Resend loses a notification, never a report.

exportPath.detail: The record never leaves our database. `notified_at IS NULL` is the query that finds every report whose notice did not go out, from any provider.

exitPlan.alternative: Amazon SES ([ADR 029] §3 names it as the documented fallback), or any provider with an HTTP send API — the body is from/to/subject/text.
exitPlan.swapCost: One function (notifyReport): a new URL, header and body shape, and one secret. No schema change, no client change, no store release.

_why: [pipeline C-4] A PACKAGE IS EARNED, NEVER NAMED. 39-CHASSIS §2 adjudicated this and it was
written nowhere that binds. A capability name is not a reason: followed loosely, the remaining
gap list would spawn packages for share, deep-links, review, purchases, connectivity and
analytics -- six pubspecs, six analysis_options, six workspace entries, six test harnesses and
six CI surfaces, forever, for one founder. Applied correctly, share_plus / app_links /
in_app_review all land in the existing platform_storage.
Keyed by PACKAGE, not capability, because two capabilities can share one package (core owns
both `core` and `analytics_funnel`) and the cost being controlled is the package.
THE ENUM IS CLOSED and each reason must SUBSTANTIATE ITSELF AGAINST THE TREE -- free text was
rejected at lock time because a justification nobody can check is a justification that always
passes:
native-binary    evidence.dependency must be declared in that package's own pubspec
licence-exposure evidence.dependency must be declared, and evidence.licence named
codegen          evidence.buildFile must exist on disk
chassis          evidence.ledgerTarget must be the destination of at least one MOVES row in
tooling/chassis-ledger.json whose measured callSiteDelta is NEGATIVE
GRANDFATHERED    predates the rule; needs declaredOn + detail, the date must be ON OR BEFORE
2026-07-28, and it PRINTS on every run
Rejections already adjudicated, recorded so no future session re-litigates them: do NOT rename
platform_storage -> platform_adapters, and do NOT merge notifications into it. Both were built
under the older reading; the rename is churn across every pubspec and import for zero
user-visible value.
`chassis` and the GRANDFATHERED date rule both arrived with [ADR 067] decision 2 / [ADR 066]
defect 1, 2026-09-05. A chassis package is not earned by being called one: it is earned by
being the measured destination of work the chassis ledger already records as a call-site
SHRINK, which is [ADR 066]'s rule and not a second copy of it. And GRANDFATHERED had never
checked what its own word meant -- a package created today, dated today, passed. It does not
now.

packages/auth_supabase.detail: Ships platform code: the secure-storage bridges and the deep-link/callback handling that completes an OAuth redirect, which differ on all six targets. It is also the ONLY package permitted to import the Supabase SDK — [2]C-5 limb (c) fails the build for any app that reaches for it directly, which is what keeps the identity provider swappable.

packages/platform_storage.detail: Keychain on iOS/macOS, KeyStore on Android, DPAPI on Windows, libsecret on Linux -- five different native implementations behind one Dart call. This is the shape that earns a package: the platform difference is real and somebody must absorb it once.

packages/notifications.detail: Native scheduling APIs per platform, and the capability genuinely differs per platform (Linux shows but cannot schedule; Windows on the pinned 17.x does neither; web has no plugin at all) -- which is why NotificationCapabilities exists at all.

packages/telemetry.detail: Ships native crash handlers -- a Dart-only reporter cannot catch a native crash, which is the class of failure this package exists for.

packages/tokens.detail: A build step, not a library: style-dictionary compiles the DTCG source at contracts/tokens/dtcg/ into three committed outputs (CSS, Dart, JSON), and ci.yml's `site-tokens` lane deletes all three, rebuilds and fails on any diff. It has no pubspec because it is a Node package.

packages/core.detail: The spine, not an earned split -- it is what the other packages are separate FROM, so the earn test does not really apply to it. Substantiates none of the three (crypto and cryptography are both pure Dart). Left grandfathered rather than given an invented reason: an exemption you can see is safer than a justification that is not true.

packages/design_system.detail: Pure Flutter widgets -- no native payload, no licence exposure, no codegen. Its real justification is the C-5 boundary (it must not be able to see the domain), which is a boundary argument rather than one of the three structural reasons. Recorded honestly instead of stretching the enum to fit.

packages/api_client.detail: dio is pure Dart, so this substantiates nothing. It is the single most likely package to be MERGED if the rule is ever applied retroactively -- kept because [2]C-3 has just moved all three dio transports into it and moving them twice would be churn.

packages/analysis.detail: A lint ruleset -- config, not code, and flutter_lints is not a native payload. It is nonetheless the one grandfathered package with a clear reason to stay separate: [2]C-12 made it the single convention set that every package, every app and the brick template inherits, so one rule edit reaches every app the factory will ever stamp. (Until 2026-07-28 it had ZERO consumers and its own include sat commented out, which is why this entry originally read 'delivers nothing'.)

packages/purchases.detail: A hosted checkout is an external URL, and opening one is a per-platform native call with real gaps -- which is why PurchaseCapabilities exists. It also has to be a package rather than app code for three requirements to be enforceable at all: assert-adapter-capabilities.mjs derives its domain from packages/ with a third-party dep, assert-no-seam-forks.mjs forbids a registered seam under apps/, and assert-no-price-literals.mjs needs the price to live behind a model. Leaving the adapter in apps/subscriptiontracker satisfied none of them while appearing to satisfy M-15 -- see [ADR 026].

packages/external_links.detail: 2026-09-24 · O-LINK-LAUNCHER-SEAM-UNOWNED. Opening an external link is a per-platform native call with real gaps (ExternalLinkCapabilities), and until this package existed the brick and apps/subscriptiontracker each imported url_launcher directly -- the two dated `|url_launcher` bypasses assert-package-boundaries.mjs printed on every run. It is a package rather than a second capability on packages/purchases because that seam, CheckoutLauncher, opens checkout pages https-only and refuses mailto: by design; hosting legal pages and the support address there would make a money seam own the privacy policy. It is not in platform_storage because the adapter must enforce core's LinkPolicy on every link, and a separate package keeps the one url_launcher import for non-checkout links in a place assert-package-boundaries limb C can name.

packages/chassis_screens.detail: [ADR 067] decision 2 / [ADR 071]. Not a name: the ledger row for lib/features/auth/reset_password_screen.dart is MOVES with a measured callSiteDelta of -233 (310 brick lines -> 77, 287 package lines added), and assert-package-earned reads THAT row rather than this sentence. The package exists because a widget that can see nikatru_core keeps the core-type-to-plain-value mapping out of the adapter -- the cost that made both design_system adoptions GROW the call site (+136, +148, [ADR 066]). It declares no third-party dependency, so assert-package-boundaries limb C never records it as an adapter wrapping a vendor.

packages/billing_revenuecat.detail: StoreKit on iOS and macOS and the Play Billing Library on Android, behind one Dart call — the platform difference is real and somebody has to absorb it once. It is a SIBLING of packages/purchases rather than a dependency OF it, and that is the measured part rather than a preference: Subly and every stamped app depend on nikatru_purchases, so declaring purchases_flutter there would link the native IAP payload into every app in the portfolio, and assert-play-declarations limb D (dependency-set EQUALITY) plus the Apple binaryInventory would then demand a sworn purchase-history row from every app at once. [ADR 078] (LOCKED 2026-09-11, amending [ADR 059] decision 10's "Shape A for v1") makes Android, iOS and the Mac App Store sell in-app at v1, so the reason is no longer "mobile is free": it is that an app which has not opted in must not link the IAP payload or swear the row UNTIL it does. An app opts IN by depending on this package and declaring billing.mobileIap in its app.yaml; assert-app-yaml limb 6 holds those two together in both directions. [ADR 067] decision 7 / [ADR 039] D5.

_why: [13]T-12 -- THE DEMAND GATE. A capability the requirements describe in full, and that must NOT
be built until an app asks for it. The habit / streak / daily-goal mechanic is the first of
them: ONE chassis module, progress tied to content mastery and never to empty points, designed
for a habit-formation horizon of ~66 days, built once when the first app that needs it is being
built and inherited thereafter -- never per app.
WHY THE DECLARATION LIVES HERE AND NOT IN THE BRICK'S `vars`. Both surfaces were considered and
the full reasoning is written at the head of the [13]T-12 section of
tooling/ci/assert-capability-register.mjs, beside the guard the choice has to serve. In short: a
brick var is consumed at STAMP time and leaves nothing on disk to quantify over, and apps/subscriptiontracker
was never stamped by this brick at all -- so a brick-var domain would exclude the only shipped
app. `consumerRoots` at the top of this file is already the machine-readable set of apps, each
verified against a real pubspec.
FIELDS.
id           the module's name. THE PRINTED LINE IS DERIVED FROM IT (`no consumer declares the
<id> module`) rather than stored as prose, so the register cannot drift from the
sentence the requirement demands.
requirement  the pipeline id that owns it.
capability   what it would be, in one sentence, so nobody has to go and look before deciding.
declaredBy   THE DEMAND, and the whole point of the row. Consumer roots (apps, or the brick
template every future app inherits from) that declare a need for the module.
EMPTY IS THE NORMAL, CORRECT STATE, and it is printed dated on every run.
module       what must then exist: the `owner` directory, the `package` name, and the
`symbols` whose declaration anywhere in the tree means the module has been built.
neverPerApp  the module may never be implemented inside apps/ or stamped per app by the brick.
Its own limb, so an app-local rebuild fails whether or not demand was declared.
BOTH DIRECTIONS FAIL THE BUILD. A module present with an empty `declaredBy` is a [2]C-2
violation -- a capability that is wired, guarded, green and useless. A non-empty `declaredBy`
with no module is the other direction, and the build stays red until the module exists as shared
code with a `capabilities` entry below that lists every declarer as a consumer.
DELIBERATELY NOT ENFORCED YET. The requirement also denylists points / xp / coins / gems /
currency / score from the module's public API. The module does not exist, so that limb has an
EMPTY DOMAIN: there is no input to this tree that could make it fail, which by this repo's own
rule is an assertion worse than none -- it inflates apparent coverage while checking nothing. It
lands with the module's first line, not before.

modules.capability: The streak / daily-goal mechanic as a single chassis module: progress tied to content mastery, never to empty points, designed for a habit-formation horizon of ~66 days.
modules.why: Demand-gated because a habit mechanic bolted onto an app that does not need one is the exact shape [2]C-2 forbids: it costs a pubspec, an analysis_options, a workspace entry, a test harness and a CI surface forever, and delivers nothing. No app in this factory declares one today -- the notifications package already carries the reminder half, which is the only piece any shipped app has needed. The moment an app declares here, the module is built ONCE, shared, and inherited.

capabilities.capability: The app-neutral spine: it DECLARES most of the factory's seam contracts, and owns config, caches and domain models. Nothing here may know about a specific app.

seams._closedGap: [13]T-9, 2026-08-07. This seam CARRIED a `missingMethods` waiver for the notification tap / open surface. It is closed, so the waiver is gone -- leaving it would have been the stale waiver its own `closedIf` clauses existed to catch, and both of them now match: the seam declares `notificationTaps()` and the adapter registers `onDidReceiveNotificationResponse`.
